_readme: Address hypotheses for roms/zelda_la_dx.gbc (gitignored, not versioned). Each entry: value/meaning, source tier, verified_count, confidence. Hardware-standard GB addresses (OAM, PPU registers) are high-confidence by architecture, not empirical hypotheses -- still logged here since the driver reads them the same way.

oam_base.meaning: 40 sprites x 4 bytes (Y, X, tile, flags); Y<160 && Y>0 means on-screen
oam_base.note: Link has NO fixed slot -- game reassigns which slot renders him between frames (confirmed session 2: same moving sprite pair seen at slot 16/17 then slot 2/3). find_link() works around this by excluding known-stationary NPC (Y,X) rather than tracking a slot.

dialogue_text_scratch_line1.meaning: Fixed scratch-buffer tile-ID range reused for dialogue line 1, regardless of speaker/content
dialogue_text_scratch_line1.note: Confirmed byte-for-byte identical across 2 different NPCs with different text -- see docs/CONCEPT.md. Decode by pixel bitmap, never by this ID.

link_position_x.meaning: Link's X coordinate, world/screen pixel units
link_position_x.note: From villager_screen checkpoint: +1/+2 per RIGHT tap (4x), -1/-2 per LEFT tap (4x), flat across 4x DOWN + 4x UP taps. Matches the community LADX disassembly's hLinkPositionX hypothesis exactly. Supersedes the OAM-based find_link() workaround as the primary position source -- see DECISIONS.md.

link_position_x_shadow.meaning: Tracks link_position_x byte-for-byte (same deltas on every RIGHT/LEFT tap) -- purpose unconfirmed (double-buffer? sub-pixel-free copy?)
link_position_x_shadow.note: Found alongside 0xFF98 in the same full-space diff; identical delta sequence on all 8 taps (4 RIGHT + 4 LEFT). Not yet needed by any consumer -- logged for completeness.

link_position_y.meaning: Link's Y coordinate, world/screen pixel units
link_position_y.note: +1/+2 per DOWN tap (4x), -1/-2 per UP tap (4x), flat across 4x RIGHT + 4x LEFT taps. Matches hLinkPositionY hypothesis.

link_direction.meaning: Facing direction, small enum (1=right seen at spawn, 3=down, 2=up observed; 0 seen transiently mid-turn)
link_direction.note: Changed exactly on a direction change (RIGHT->DOWN->UP), stable while repeating the same direction. Left-value not yet observed directly -- infer from the enum pattern, don't assume without a dedicated LEFT-only check.

room_id.meaning: Current room/screen identifier -- NOT globally unique by itself, see collision below
room_id.note: front_yard=162, overworld_screen2=178, villager_screen=177, screen3_north=161, shop_screen=179, house2_interior=169, starting_house=163 (map_id=16), room160=160/map0 (new, west of 161, unexplored past entry -- see world_topology.room161_exits_and_sprites). COLLISION found September 8, 2026 (Explorer subagent, exploring east of front_yard, observed twice independently in separate script runs): a new outdoor room directly east of front_yard also reads room_id=163, but map_id=0 -- distinct from starting_house's map_id=16 at the same room_id. (room_id, map_id) is the real key, room_id alone is not. room_id=177/map_id=0 re-confirmed September 8, 2026 via real navigation (front_yard_to_room177 below), matching legacy's old villager_screen checkpoint's room_id. Supersedes ScreenGrid's discovery-order screen names as the canonical room key -- see DECISIONS.md.

map_id.meaning: Coarser than room_id -- looks like an overworld/interior (or dungeon) discriminator, not a full map index. Combined with room_id, forms the actual unique room key -- see room_id's note above.
map_id.note: 0 on every overworld screen checked (7, now including the 3 new rooms west/east/south of front_yard), 16 on the one interior (house2_interior/starting_house). Only 2 distinct values seen so far -- can't yet distinguish 'overworld' from 'a specific interior/dungeon number' with just one interior sample.

link_position.ruled_out_reason: Isolated via 4x consistent-small-positive-delta diff on RIGHT taps (strong signal, see method below), but a follow-up RIGHT/LEFT/DOWN cross-check showed all 4 increase on every tap regardless of direction -- animation-frame or step counters, not an (X,Y) coordinate. A true X byte would decrease on LEFT; none did.
link_position.method_for_next_attempt: This WRAM-only search (0xC000-0xDFFF) was the mistake: the review docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md flagged that neither memory hunt had ever scanned HRAM (0xFF80-0xFFFE). A full 0x0000-0xFFFF diff (see legacy/game_agents/experiments/ram_diff_hram.rb and its ram_diff_hram2.rb cross-validation follow-up) found the real coordinates there in one pass. The same full-space-diff technique is what the terrain-collision-in-WRAM question should reuse.
link_position.accepted_workaround: OBSOLETE now that hram.link_position_x/y are verified -- kept as history, not to be reused. find_link() via OAM exclusion was sufficient for the mapping tool but is exactly the wrong-layer approach the review calls out.

intro_door_gate.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-08 -- confirmed legitimate shield-gating, not a bug. Not a RAM address entry; kept here for provenance continuity with the investigation above.
intro_door_gate.note: Confirmed, not just hypothesized: got the shield through a real conversation with Tarkin (lib/navigator.rb, D7) and walked to the south door -- zero blocking, zero 'Hé mon gars' message. The door was always legitimately shield-gated; front_yard's approach to Tarkin (target y:80,x:112) had been abandoned early by a known legacy/ bug (root_cause_2026_09_07_night below), so the shield was never obtained and the block looked like a mystery gate. The 0xD3E7/0xDFF9 flags recorded in the previous entry (method_2026_09_07_evening, kept below for the record) were noise from the door NPC's dialogue box opening, as suspected -- not re-examined further, no longer relevant now the real mechanism is confirmed.
intro_door_gate.root_cause_2026_09_07_night: Checked Link's actual OAM position against the two stationary NPCs at the before_shield_gift checkpoint (reading via MMU#debug_read, gemboy PR #9, to bypass a PPU-bus-gating artifact that made legacy/primitives.rb's oam_sprites return an empty list at this exact frame): Link at (74,82)/(74,90), the likely-Tarkin NPC pair at (80,120)/(80,128) -- a 38px gap, nowhere near adjacent. front_yard's approach loops break early because move_tiles's own 'moved' count under-reports: 6 manual :right taps from this checkpoint each returned moved=0 while x visibly advanced by 2px per tap (82->84->86->...->94) -- the long-documented 'creeping collision' undercount (see scenarios.rb's house2_interior comment for the same pattern elsewhere). front_yard's loops treat moved=0 as 'blocked, try something else' and give up on approaching Tarkin long before actually reaching him. No shield is ever given; the door NPC blocking Link afterward is correct game logic, not a bug or a gate to bypass.
intro_door_gate.method_2026_09_07_evening_superseded: Isolated the door-block trigger itself (proximity-based, fires at y=122->121 with a backward reposition, dialogue 'Hé mon gars, attends un peu !') and diffed WRAM+HRAM+OAM+IO around it: 195 bytes changed, mostly dialogue-render state (0xD500-0xD616, matching wram_unmapped.room_object_grid's earlier same-room diff) and audio registers. Flagged 0xD3E7/0xDFF9 as gate-condition candidates -- superseded by the same-night finding above: this dialogue is the door NPC correctly reacting to Link not having the shield, not a special gate state.
intro_door_gate.not_worth_fixing_in_legacy: D5 says legacy/ is replaced, not extended; move_tiles's creeping-collision undercount is exactly the class of primitive D7's snapshot-based tool is meant to replace properly. Reaching Tarkin is deferred to Session 2's new lib/ navigation tool rather than patched here.

room_object_grid.status: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-08 -- the signal exists, but in VRAM's existing BG tilemap, not a separate WRAM buffer. See terrain_collision.background_tilemap_predicts_walkability below.
room_object_grid.note: Session 1 hypothesis (docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md's next question): a per-room 16x16 object grid in WRAM whose type-per-cell predicts collision. Brute-forced every (base address in 0xC000-0xDFFF, stride in [8,9,10,16,20], row-major/col-major) against the starting_house oracle grid (legacy/.../screen_maps/starting_house.json, 32 cells with edges, 123 direction-edge samples, 28 blocked/95 ok) using a single-byte-value classifier. Best candidates: 80.5% accuracy vs a 77.2% majority-class baseline, using degenerate marker values (0, 255) that are common noise anywhere in RAM -- not a credible signal.
room_object_grid.why_inconclusive_not_refuted: Tested against only one room (front_yard, the second room the criterion calls for, is blocked -- see intro_door_gate's related_finding above). A single static snapshot can't isolate a candidate the way D1's method did (diff between two different rooms to find the block that changes); with only one room, most of WRAM is trivially 'consistent' with almost any single-cell hypothesis by chance. Re-test once a second room is reachable, using the diff-between-rooms method NEXT.md originally specified, before concluding either way on D4.

front_yard_adjacent_rooms.status: 4 directions now characterized (not just 3+1) -- two isolated Explorer subagents plus this session's own follow-up capture, September 8, 2026, real navigation via Koholint::Navigator from /tmp/zelda_checkpoints/front_yard_navigator.dump, no assumed game knowledge.
front_yard_adjacent_rooms.note: West: room_id=161/map_id=0 (re-confirms the pre-existing single-observation screen3_north note). East: room_id=163/map_id=0, observed twice independently -- see hram.room_id's collision note, this is NOT starting_house despite sharing room_id. South (tested from two different entry columns, same result both times): room_id=178/map_id=0 (re-confirms the pre-existing overworld_screen2 note; re-confirmed a 3rd time, September 8, 2026, via full traversal through it, not just entry -- see front_yard_to_room177 below). North: CORRECTED, September 8, 2026 (second Explorer subagent, only 2 of ~9 columns had been tested when this entry first said 'confirmed genuine wall') -- front_yard has a real corridor at its far-west columns 0-1, not a sealed north edge. Column 1 (x<=24) walks all the way to the top with no blocks and transitions into room_id=146/map_id=0, a genuinely new room, confirmed both by the subagent (14 consecutive Navigator.move! calls, all :ok) and independently reproduced by this session directly (Navigator.tap loop, x:88->24 west then y:131->88 crossing into room 146 -- see NEXT.md for the gif). Column 0 stops one tile short of the same breakthrough point, blocked by a single discrete BG-tile obstacle at the screen's top-left corner (tile signature {26,27,36,37}, distinct from the room's hedge-wall signature {0c,0c,1c,1c}; no OAM sprite at that position in a 40-slot scan, so it's a background tile obstacle, not a sprite -- visually tree-like per the owner's direct description, not independently confirmed as literally a 'tree' beyond that visual read). Columns 2,3,4,7,8 all hit a different, real obstacle: a straight hedge wall at y=122 (mid-screen, not the top edge) -- same wall column 5 was already known to run into. Column 6 is not an independent data point: it drifted to column 5's x mid-walk (a game alignment effect), merging into the already-known door-loop path. None of the 4 new rooms (161, 163/map0, 178, 146) have been explored beyond their entry point -- no item/NPC/story beat confirmed, only visually-distinct unverified sprite content per room: west/161 has a house-like structure, tan block objects, and a rounded green creature-like sprite; east/163-map0 is an undifferentiated repeating clover/bush field, no distinguishing feature found yet; south/178 has a circular hedge/fence ring around a centered rounded green creature-like sprite plus two small sprites reading as airborne -- the only non-rectangular, deliberately-shaped layout of the four, and the subagent's recommended next room to chart on that basis. Tile IDs/sprite shapes are reported by appearance only, never assumed to be a specific named object per AGENTS.md's forbidden-game-knowledge rule.

room177_sprites.status: confirmed -- isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, real OAM diffs and a proximity-gated :a interaction test with a negative control, from room 177 (see front_yard_to_room177 above for how it's reached).
room177_sprites.note: Room 177 has 2 OAM sprite pairs (flags=0x21 both) beyond Link, PLUS a lone single-tile companion sprite (tile=38, flags=0) that tracks near the wandering pair without being part of its 2-tile group -- not established whether it's decoration, a shadow/dust effect, or a distinct entity. Pair 1, originally at (y=32,x=77/85): confirmed to translate position autonomously with zero Link input (idle 60-frame test: x crept 77->106, y stayed ~32-34) -- wanders on its own, not a proximity reaction. CONFIRMED interactive, September 8, 2026 (second Explorer subagent, tap-by-tap adaptive chase closing to genuine adjacency in 24 taps) -- see dialogues.room177_wandering_sprite. Pair 2, at (y=96,x=120/128): stayed at that exact position across every sample and 2 independent approach angles (13 move! steps) -- genuinely static, only its tile ID flickers (animation, not translation). Also interactive -- see dialogues.room177_static_sprite. BOTH pairs are interactive with the SAME dialogue text -- 'moves on its own' was not a useful predictor of interactivity either way here, both sprites in this room happen to be interactive. Methodological notes for reuse: both pairs' OAM entries alternate between two disjoint slot ranges frame-to-frame (same slot-reassignment behavior already documented for Link in legacy/primitives.rb) -- identify a sprite by position/exclusion, never a fixed OAM slot number. Facing direction matters as much as raw proximity for triggering :a -- face the sprite's dominant approach axis immediately before pressing :a, not just get pixel-adjacent.

room177_exits.status: confirmed, all 4 directions -- isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, real Navigator.move! loops (10-15 calls/direction), room_id/map_id checked after every call.
room177_exits.note: East: 4 clean :ok steps then transitions to room_id=178/map_id=0 (re-confirms the known entry path). North: blocked near the spawn column/x=100 (the building's own footprint, not the room edge), but from x=140 (clear of the building) it's 8 consecutive :ok steps then transitions to room_id=161/map_id=0 -- confirms 161 borders BOTH front_yard (west side) and room177 (north side), making 161 a hub, not a dead-end. West: blocked near the building at x=100/spawn row, but wide open at y=106 (below the building) for 12 steps down to x=44, then 1 more step to x=36 where it hits a genuine, consistently-reproduced wall (14 more calls, zero progress, re-tested from two approach angles) -- no transition, real boundary. South: blocked at y=112 independently at 3 separate columns (x=36, x=100, x=140) -- same y every time, strong evidence of one straight wall/hedge spanning the room's width, not a per-column artifact -- no transition, real boundary. Lesson: don't test a direction from a column/row that happens to graze the building sprite's footprint and conclude 'wall' -- both false negatives here (north near spawn, west near spawn row) turned into real open exits once tested from a column/row clear of the building.

room161_exits_and_sprites.status: confirmed, all 4 directions plus a new room found -- isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, real Navigator.move! loops (10-15 calls, multiple columns/rows per direction after an initial false-negative near the house's footprint).
room161_exits_and_sprites.note:
room_id=161/map_id=0 is a genuine 3-way hub: East -> front_yard (162/0, 4 calls, known). South -> room177 (177/0, 1 call, known -- room177's own north exit). North -> genuine wall at y=26, confirmed identically at 3 separate columns (x=20,116,132) spanning the room's width; two closer columns (x=36,52) gave a false stop at y=74 first -- that's the house's own footprint, not the room edge, same false-negative pattern as room177's building. West -> a NEW room, room_id=160/map_id=0, found via a mid-height row (y=99, 13 calls) -- NOT the whole west edge though: the bottom row (y=131) hits a real wall at x=20 with no transition, the doorway to 160 is a specific gap. room160 (unexplored past entry): a visually distinct area -- raised stone/hedge platform around a well/altar-like structure, a water/river tile pattern on its west edge, flower sprites, a green blob-creature sprite.
Interaction: extensively tested, no dialogue found on any of room161's sprites (~32 :a attempts total). At least 3 distinct moving/animated OAM entities beyond Link: (1) a round green 'blob' 2-tile mirrored pair (tile family 0x70-0x7C) wandering the lower-left -- chased to 1-3px adjacency from 3 angles with correct facing, 9 attempts, zero dialogue; (2) an 'ear'-shaped creature (tile family 0x58-0x5C) wandering widely, sometimes above the confirmed north wall (y<26, likely unreachable/decorative there) -- 5 clean adjacency attempts, zero dialogue; (3) a vertical 2-tile post/standing object (tile=0x7E both halves, unusual vertical not horizontal stacking) near the house -- chase script cross-tracked onto other sprites before achieving verified adjacency, INCONCLUSIVE not refuted. A positive control (room177's already-confirmed sprite, same session, same :a mechanism) DID open its known dialogue -- confirms the negative results in 161 are real, not a broken test. The house structure itself was not probed for a door/entry point. Lesson for reuse: a chase script that re-targets by 'nearest surviving pair to the previous frame' can silently jump between distinct same-shaped sprites when several are close together (observed here) -- tighten max-jump distance and/or require tile-ID equality between paired halves.

front_yard_to_room177.status: confirmed -- isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, real navigation via Koholint::Navigator.move! from front_yard_navigator.dump, testing legacy scenarios.rb's old villager_screen hint (direction only, not its tap counts -- legacy's move_tiles-based counts don't map onto move!'s tile-calibrated steps).
front_yard_to_room177.note: Path: front_yard (162/0) -[south]-> 178/0 -[~2-3 more down steps, then a wall]-> -[~10-11 left steps]-> room_id=177/map_id=0, entered at x=140,y=48 facing right. 16 Navigator.move! calls total, 2 real room transitions. room_id=177 matches legacy's old villager_screen checkpoint's room_id -- the legacy DIRECTION hint (south then west/left) held up; its exact tap counts (40 down, 44 left) did not, confirming direction-only is the reusable part of a legacy hint. IMPORTANT Navigator.move! caveat found here, now noted in lib/navigator.rb: on the exact step that crosses a room boundary, move! can return :blocked even though a real transition happened -- position() rebases onto the new screen, so the pre/post delta on the old axis reads under COMMIT_THRESHOLD. Both transitions on this path (front_yard->178 and 178->177) hit this -- room_id/map_id must be checked after every move! call near a screen edge, never inferred from :ok/:blocked alone. Room 177 OAM snapshot (single frame, 7 on-screen slots beyond background): Link at slots 2/3 (y=48,x=140/148); two 2-tile sprite pairs, flags=0x21, at (y=96,x=120/128) and (y=32,x=77/85); one single-tile sprite at (y=44,x=81) -- not yet confirmed whether any of these move (would distinguish an animated/interactable sprite from static decoration), proposed as the next question. Room not yet explored beyond its entry point.

background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.status: confirmed, cross-checked in 2 rooms (starting_house, front_yard) -- an isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, then ratified as D8 (DECISIONS.md) and implemented as lib/terrain.rb + lib/validation/terrain_predictor_check.rb the same day.
background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.method: Read the active BG tilemap (hardware.bg_tilemap_0/1, selected by hardware.lcdc bit 0x08, via mmu.debug_read to bypass PPU bus-gating) and map cell (row,col) [= world y/16, x/16, the oracle grid's own convention] directly to the 2x2 tile-ID block at tilemap rows {2*row,2*row+1}, cols {2*col,2*col+1} -- no SCX/SCY scroll correction applied or needed in either sampled state (both had SCX=SCY=0).
background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.finding: In both rooms, every oracle-confirmed-walkable cell's 2x2 tile-ID block and every oracle-confirmed-blocked-target cell's block partition into two disjoint sets with zero full-block overlap: starting_house (37 walkable / 18 blocked cells) uses ~2 floor signatures vs ~9 wall signatures; front_yard (25 walkable / 8 blocked cells) uses 6 floor/path signatures vs 2 wall signatures. The partition is per-room/per-tileset categorical, not a single global numeric threshold across rooms (no 'tile ID >= 0x80 means solid' rule holds in both) -- likely a ROM-side per-tile-ID lookup table keyed by tileset, not a per-room WRAM buffer. Supersedes wram_unmapped.room_object_grid's WRAM-buffer hypothesis: the signal exists, just in the wrong memory region from what Session 1 searched.
caveats: Granularity: a couple of single tile IDs (0x0A/0x0B, 0x7F in starting_house) appear in both a walkable and a blocked 2x2 block, but only at genuine doorway/wall-base boundaries where a 16px oracle cell straddles an 8px tile boundary -- collision plausibly resolves at 8x8 tile granularity, not the 16x16 cell grid the oracle/Navigator use. Not a contradiction of the finding, but means a literal cell-level lookup needs care at boundaries.

Directional asymmetry: front_yard cell (6,3) has the room's own unambiguous wall tile signature ({0C,0C,1C,1C}), yet Koholint::Navigator.move! reached it via a LEFT approach and reported the (5,3)<->(6,3) boundary open from below -- while the static oracle recorded (5,3)'s 'down' edge as blocked. Read as a one-way ledge (walkable from one side only), not a refutation -- but means a pure tile-ID lookup alone won't fully replace directional probing without also encoding one-way edges.

SCX/SCY=0 held in every state sampled this session (both checkpoints, plus after 8 real moves in front_yard), but front_yard is a scrolling room -- the no-scroll-correction formula is unverified further from the door/spawn area and should be re-checked before relying on it room-wide.
background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.builder_validation_2026_09_08: lib/validation/terrain_predictor_check.rb: a RoomClassifier that caches walkable/blocked verdict per tile-ID signature (Link's own cell is a free walkable sample; a genuinely new signature costs one Navigator live probe to learn, then every future cell sharing it is free) reproduced the same breadth-first full-coverage sweep as oracle_grid_check.rb. Result: 161/173 (93.1%) combined agreement (up from the pure-live-probe sweep's 145/173), using only 22 total live probes (vs up to 8 taps x 173 edges for the pure-probe method) -- front_yard reached 60/60 (100%) with 9 probes; starting_house reached 101/113 with 13 probes. The 12 remaining starting_house disagreements are an exact subset of the pure-live-probe sweep's own 'oracle=blocked, real movement=ok' disagreements (cross-checked cell-by-cell against NEXT.md's prior session report) -- two independent methods (live movement, static tile read) agree with each other and disagree with the same static legacy oracle, in the same direction, which is stronger evidence the oracle is stale there than that either live method is wrong. None of the pure-probe sweep's 9 'oracle=ok, Navigator=blocked' false negatives survive in the terrain method.

dialogues._readme: Confirmed dialogue text, transcribed from rendered framebuffers (dialogue is drawn via the BG tilemap, not stored as readable memory strings -- 0xD0-0xDF/0xE0-0xEF are tile IDs, confirmed to read all-zero even while a real dialogue box is visibly open on screen; NEVER trust that address range as a dialogue-state flag, always render and read visually). One entry per confirmed interactable, with the room/position/trigger that produced it.

room177_static_sprite.sprite_oam_position: (y=96, x=120/128), 2-tile pair, flags=0x21 -- see world_topology.room177_sprites for full sprite context (this is the STATIC one, not the wandering one)

room177_static_sprite.text: YOUPI! J'ai la pêche! Et toi?
room177_static_sprite.note: Text CORRECTED September 8, 2026 -- the original transcription read as all-caps ('YOUPI! J'AI LA PECHE! ET TOI?'), but a second independent capture (dialogues.room177_wandering_sprite, same text) zoomed the rendered framebuffer and confirmed real mixed case with a circumflex accent on the e in 'pêche'.
